tooltip.title: Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) for the Dermatologist
tooltip.markdown: PsA is a seronegative inflammatory arthritis strongly associated with psoriasis. Dermatologists are on the front line for early detection, as skin disease precedes arthritis in ~85% of cases. \[24\]

tooltip.title: Screening for PsA in Psoriasis Patients
tooltip.markdown: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent irreversible joint damage. Dermatologists should screen psoriasis patients regularly.

tooltip.title: The "PSA" Mnemonic
tooltip.markdown:
A simple tool to remember key symptoms:

-   **P:** Pain in joints
-   **S:** Stiffness (especially morning stiffness >30 min) / Swelling / Sausage digit
-   **A:** Axial (inflammatory back pain)

tooltip.title: Validated Screening Questionnaires
tooltip.markdown: Tools like the PEST (Psoriasis Epidemiology Screening Tool) can be used in the clinic to identify patients at high risk who require referral to a rheumatologist.

tooltip.title: The Domains of PsA
tooltip.markdown: PsA is a heterogeneous disease that can affect multiple musculoskeletal sites.

tooltip.title: Peripheral Arthritis
tooltip.markdown: Inflammation of joints in the limbs. Can be oligoarticular (<5 joints) or polyarticular (≥5 joints), and is often asymmetric.

tooltip.title: Axial Disease
tooltip.markdown: Inflammation of the spine (spondylitis) and sacroiliac joints (sacroiliitis), causing inflammatory back pain.

tooltip.title: Enthesitis
tooltip.markdown: Inflammation at the site of tendon or ligament insertion into bone. Classic locations include the Achilles tendon and plantar fascia insertion on the heel.

tooltip.title: Dactylitis ("Sausage Digit")
tooltip.markdown: Inflammation of the entire digit (finger or toe), including the joint, tendon, and soft tissue, leading to diffuse swelling.

tooltip.title: Skin and Nail Disease
tooltip.markdown: The presence of psoriasis, particularly nail psoriasis (pitting, onycholysis), is a key feature and a risk factor for developing PsA.
